text.text: The remaining 14, and what each needs beyond (E, A, Y ): • Demographic parity, equalized odds, intersectional analysis: a trained classifier's predictions.

Demographic parity is the difference in positive prediction rate between groups, equalized odds the largest difference in TPR or FPR, and intersectional analysis the same gaps over combinations of attributes.
They are properties of a trained classifier; of the three, only the equalized-odds gaps (TPR and FPR) are reported in this paper, for the heads of Section 4.3.
• GroupDRO [66], GCE [67], early-epoch clustering (SPARE): training a model and access to its loss or representations during training.
text.formatted: • GroupDRO <ref type="bibr" target="#b65">[66]</ref>, GCE <ref type="bibr" target="#b66">[67]</ref>, early-epoch clustering (SPARE): training a model and access to its loss or representations during training.

text.text: • SSA: a split into attribute-labelled and unlabelled data.
• CAV: user-defined concept examples.
SpRAy [68] and GradCAM mask overlap [69]: images and model gradients.
text.formatted: SpRAy <ref type="bibr" target="#b67">[68]</ref> and GradCAM mask overlap <ref type="bibr" target="#b68">[69]</ref>: images and model gradients.

text.text: • Causal effect estimation [70, 71], generative CVAE, VAE disentanglement: training an auxiliary model.
text.formatted: • Causal effect estimation <ref type="bibr" target="#b69">[70,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b70">71]</ref>, generative CVAE, VAE disentanglement: training an auxiliary model.

text.text: • SIS: the current implementation searches for sufficient subsets for the task label, with a fixed subset fraction of 15%.
It has no attributeaware form and was removed from the score.
Shortcut masking: The embedding dimensions with the largest loading on the attribute direction (the top 5% here) are set to zero, randomised or inpainted.
The method works on the embeddings themselves and needs no retraining.
For image-level pipelines, foreground objects are swapped across backgrounds so that background and label are no longer correlated.
It needs segmentation masks or a foreground extractor.
Adversarial debiasing: Adversarial training with a gradient reversal layer removes group information from the learned representation [72, 73].
text.formatted: Adversarial debiasing: Adversarial training with a gradient reversal layer removes group information from the learned representation <ref type="bibr" target="#b71">[72,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b72">73]</ref>.

text.text: An adversary tries to predict A from E, and the debiasing network is trained to raise the adversary's loss while keeping task performance.
A Right for the Right Reasons regularisation term, added to the training loss, penalises model attention on detected shortcut regions.
Only the final classification layer is retrained, on a group-balanced subset of the data [54].
text.formatted: Only the final classification layer is retrained, on a group-balanced subset of the data <ref type="bibr" target="#b53">[54]</ref>.

text.text: The method is cheap to run and suited to the case where the attribute is encoded in the representation and the head gives it too much weight.
It leaves the embedding unchanged and, in Section 4.3, lowered the TPR gap at a cost in task AUROC.

Contrastive debiasing: A contrastive loss pulls together representations from different demographic groups within the same task class [74], so that the groups become less separable while the task classes stay apart.
text.formatted: Contrastive debiasing: A contrastive loss pulls together representations from different demographic groups within the same task class <ref type="bibr" target="#b73">[74]</ref>, so that the groups become less separable while the task classes stay apart.

text.text: Of these, shortcut masking, adversarial debiasing, last-layer retraining and contrastive debiasing work on frozen embeddings.
They were run with the package defaults and are evaluated in Section 4.3.
Background randomisation and explanation regularisation need images or model gradients and were not evaluated.
Seeds, permutation counts, run times and the configuration of every stage are documented in the repository, with the run manifests from which each table and figure was regenerated.
The generator draws y i ∼ Bernoulli(0.5) and sets a i = y i with probability ρ and a i = 1 -y i otherwise.
The embedding has d coordinates drawn from N (0, 1).
A block of k y = 4 task dimensions is shifted by ±µ y /2 according to y i , with µ y = 1.0.

A disjoint block of k a = 4 attribute dimensions carries the attribute signal: • Linear: each attribute dimension is shifted by +δ/2 for a i = 1 and -δ/2 for a i = 0, so the standardised mean difference is exactly δ in each dimension and the Mahalanobis distance over the block is √ k a δ.

An L2 logistic head on standardised embeddings is trained on a subsample with P (Y = 1 | A = 1) = 0.9 and P (Y = 1 | A = 0) = 0.1 (ρ train = 0.9), and tested on a patient-disjoint subsample with all four (A, Y ) groups of equal size (ρ = 0.5).

Patients are first split in half, stratified on the image-level (A, Y ) labels with patients as groups (scikit-learn's StratifiedGroupKFold), so every image of a patient falls in one half, with a different split for each seed.
The subsamples below draw images within each (A, Y ) cell of a half.

In the training half the (A, Y ) groups (1, 1) and (0, 0) each hold 0.45N images and (1, 0) and (0, 1) each hold 0.05N , with N the largest size that the smallest group allows, so N changes with the split.
Training sets held 42 to 272 images (24 to 124 patients), and test sets 60 to 404 images (40 to 153 patients).
